name: Secrets Manager client
purpose: The one place in the project that reads secret material. Loads the manifest slice for the current deployable at boot, materialises credentials for exactly that slice through a vendor adapter, exposes a fixed named-verb surface to callers, and emits an audit event on every fetch attempt. Every other module in the project reads secrets through this client; nothing else imports the vendor SDK.
responsibilities: Load the manifest for the repo root and pick out the slice for the boot-input deployable id (AC-8101-1, AC-8103-1).
Refuse `get`/`getRequired` for a name outside the declared slice with a stable-coded `SECRETS_OUT_OF_SLICE` error and no vendor call (AC-8101-2, AC-8103-1).

Materialise vendor credentials once at boot for exactly the declared slice; refuse boot on a required-absent secret with `SECRETS_REQUIRED_ABSENT` naming the logical name and active environment (AC-8102-2, AC-8108-1, AC-8107-3).
Serve `get(name)` from an in-memory cache; support `refresh()` as an atomic swap so a concurrent `get` never sees a mixed slice (AC-8102-3).

Emit exactly one structured audit event per fetch attempt, with fields `name`, `path`, `environment`, `principal`, `outcome`, `at`; no field may carry the secret value or a substring of it (AC-8104-1, AC-8104-2, AC-8104-3).
Select the active environment from an unambiguous boot input; refuse boot on ambiguous inputs with `SECRETS_ENV_AMBIGUOUS` (AC-8107-2).
Retry-once semantics at boot: a required-absent read is attempted once, not looped (AC-8108-3).
internalStructure: One stateless class per process with an injected vendor adapter and an injected audit sink. The cache is a Map keyed by logical name and populated at boot; a refresh swaps a new Map in atomically. The vendor adapter is a project-authored module implementing the port defined in the interfaces block; the reference default vendor is named in ADR-902 and lives under the same package as this client.

interfaces.name: vendorAdapter
interfaces.description: Project-supplied vendor binding implementing `readMany({ paths, credentials, environment })` returning `{ [name]: { value, lastRotatedAt } }` or an entry-level not-found marker, and `materialiseCredentials({ slicePaths, environment })` returning per-slice credentials the vendor deny-by-default enforces.

interfaces.name: manifest
interfaces.description: The manifest loader (TAC-902) resolving the current deployable's slice, per-environment paths, and `required` flags.

interfaces.name: auditSink
interfaces.description: Structured-event sink invoked with `{ name, path, environment, principal, outcome, at }` on every fetch attempt; never invoked with the secret value.

interfaces.name: envSelector
interfaces.description: The boot-input resolver for the active environment: a process variable, a boot flag, or a project-authored selector. Returns exactly one environment string or refuses ambiguity.

dependencies.name: Secrets Manifest
dependencies.description: Upstream source of the declared slice and per-environment path map the client resolves at boot.

tradeoffs: The client holds every declared value in memory for the lifetime of the process; a heap dump of a compromised process exposes the slice's cleartext. That trade means every read is a memory access rather than a vendor round trip, which is what makes the hot path affordable and what makes `refresh` cheap. Projects that want per-fetch vendor reads (short-lived credential floors, HSM-mediated flows) supply a vendor adapter whose `readMany` proxies to the vendor on every call and rely on the cache being a thin write-through layer.
